0.0.n: 戦車道 is the fictional tank-based martial art's name; 道 suggests a disciplined practice.

0.1.n: に marks what the girls devote their youth to.

0.2.n: 青春 refers to the youthful period of life, often associated with passion and dreams.

0.3.n: を marks 青春 as what they devote; English supplies the possessive, which Japanese leaves unstated.

0.4.n: かける describes committing something precious; the phrase before 女子高生 tells us which girls.

0.5.n: 女子高生 combines female students with high school status.

0.6.n: たち makes the preceding noun explicitly refer to a group.

0.7.n: を marks the girls as the people depicted.

0.8.n: 描いた is the past form of 描く and describes the title that follows.

1.1.n: ガールズ is borrowed from English and forms part of the series title.

1.3.n: パンツァー is the German word for tank, used here as part of the series title.

2.0.n: 鉄 gives the maidens a metaphorical association with strength and their tanks.

2.1.n: の links 鉄 to 乙女, giving the image of maidens of iron.

2.2.n: 乙女 is a poetic term for young women, fitting the dramatic narration.

2.3.n: たち indicates that multiple maidens are meant.

2.4.n: の links the maidens to their battle.

2.5.n: 最後 identifies this as the concluding battle.

2.6.n: の lets 最後 describe the following noun 戦い.

2.7.n: 戦い is the noun related to 戦う, to fight.

2.8.n: が marks the final battle as what will begin in line 4.

3.0.n: 全 means all or total, and 話 counts episodes here.

3.1.n: の connects the episode count to the series it describes.

3.2.n: 完全 strengthens 新作, emphasizing that the production is entirely new.

3.3.n: 新作 refers to a newly made work, here the animated series.

3.4.n: OVA is an animation release category traditionally associated with direct-to-video productions.

3.5.n: シリーズ is an English loanword referring to the connected set of episodes.

3.6.n: として identifies the format in which the final battle will be presented.

4.0.n: この directly modifies a noun, here 冬.

4.1.n: この冬 gives the time when the series begins, without needing a particle.

4.3.n: いよいよ builds excitement for a long-awaited event about to happen.

4.4.n: 始まります is the polite nonpast form of 始まる; the winter timing makes it future here.

0.lit: Depicted high school girls who devote their youth to the art of tank combat,
0.tip: The phrase ending in 描いた describes the title in the next line.

1.tip: The brackets 『 』 mark the name of a work.

2.lit: The maidens of iron's final battle,
2.tip: が marks the subject, but its verb does not arrive until line 4.

3.lit: As an entirely new OVA series of six episodes in total,
3.tip: として means as, introducing the format of the upcoming release.

4.lit: This winter, at last, will begin!
4.tip: 始まります means something begins, rather than someone starts something.
